svg.text: What a plan page has to do with type: a name you scan in a second, a time you trust, a button you can't misread.
Priya is on the way since 5:50, about 8 min.
Maybes turn into can't at 2:00 PM (in 3 h).
Only people who've shared a plan with Priya can see this. No fines, no scores, just the record.
Source Serif 4 · 400 / 600 / italic · optical size 8–60 · Google Fonts

g.text: • A sans for everything you act on, a serif for everything you read. Buttons, counts, labels and times are Space Grotesk;
sentences and names are Source Serif 4. The split itself carries meaning: if it's sans, you can tap it or it's a number.
• Space Grotesk has a tall x-height and wide, open counters, so "6:01" and "8 min" stay legible at 14 px on a phone held at arm's length,
and its slightly odd letterforms (the g, the a) give the app a character that isn't "default system app".
• Source Serif 4 at 17 px for body: a serif reads as calmer and more personal than a sans at paragraph length, which fits an app about friends,
and its optical sizes keep the small 14 px explanations crisp instead of spindly.
• Only three sizes matter: plan title (1.35 rem, 700), body (1 rem), and small print (0.85–0.9 rem). Section headings are small uppercase
tracked labels in the muted colour, so they organize without competing with the names, which are the real content.
• Weight does the emphasis, not size. Names are 600, counts are 700, everything else is 400. Nothing is bold "for decoration".
Inspiration: transit departure boards (one sans, big numbers, nothing decorative); restaurant receipts (tracked uppercase section labels on warm paper);
printed invitations (serif body with a single bold sans line for the thing that matters).
